answer: Admission proof-of-work: before an identity may join, it must solve a hash puzzle that burns real compute, like a toll paid at the wharf before mooring. One honest agent pays once, but a Sybil farm of 10,000 fakes pays 10,000 tolls, so attack cost scales linearly with headcount. Jury grading adds a second cost: every fake must also write ivory-grade original text each epoch, or its standing sinks like a hull on the reef.
